interest: This file is exceptionally valuable for historians of World War II intelligence, Axis diplomatic maneuverings, and the transition into early Cold War intelligence collection. It provides a rare, detailed view of Major General Makoto Onodera's clandestine network in Stockholm, the Imperial Japanese Army's primary listening post in neutral Northern Europe. Most notably, it offers Onodera's firsthand account of the May 1945 peace overtures mediated through Swedish businessman and Allied double agent Eric Erickson and Prince Carl of the Swedish Red Cross, providing an essential counterpoint to Allied intelligence records. Furthermore, the file illuminates the operational mechanics of Japanese military attachés across wartime Europe, revealing secret pre-war Japanese-Abwehr joint sabotage and fifth-column plans against the Soviet Caucasus and Ukraine, as well as the shadowy milieu of Axis espionage, Hungarian intelligence collaboration, black market finance, and postwar safehaven plotting involving figures such as Momotaro Enomoto and Richard Kauder (Klatt).
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.20258) contains records from late 1946 regarding Japanese wartime military intelligence, espionage networks, and diplomatic activities in Europe, centered on Major General Makoto Onodera, former Japanese Military Attaché in Stockholm. The file opens with a National Archives withdrawal notice for a classified August 1946 item and a November 1946 despatch from George Atcheson, Jr., U.S. Political Adviser for Japan in Tokyo, reporting that a Swedish Foreign Office request to interrogate Onodera should be answered from existing Strategic Services Unit (SSU) interrogation reports rather than putting new questions to him in Sugamo Prison. The remainder of the file comprises a December 1946 Central Intelligence Group (CIG) memorandum transmitting three detailed intelligence reports (DB-1244, DB-1245, and DB-1247) compiled from Onodera's debriefings. These reports disclose Onodera's version of the May–July 1945 Japanese-Swedish peace initiatives involving Allied double agent Eric Erickson and Prince Carl; the organizational hierarchy, targets, and joint sabotage operations of Japanese military attachés in Europe against the USSR; and an intelligence assessment of Japanese correspondent Momotaro Enomoto, examining his clandestine ties to Japanese nationalist Han Wakabayashi, the German Abwehr, and the Hungarian intelligence service.

subfiles.about: A National Archives withdrawal sheet recording the removal of a security-classified item dated August 30, 1946, addressed to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: This General Services Administration document withdrawal notice (GSA Form 7117) records the removal of document No. 233, dated August 30, 1946, from file designation 894.20258/8-3046. The item was removed during archive review on April 20, 1976, because it contains security-classified information under general and specific National Archives record group restriction statements. The document was addressed to Tokyo, and the form bears the notation 'Sweden / No business'.
subfiles.title: Document Withdrawal Notice for File 894.20258/8-3046

subfiles.about: Despatch recommending against presenting Swedish Foreign Office interrogatories to General Makoto Onodera because existing SSU interrogation reports already answer the questions.
subfiles.summary: George Atcheson, Jr., United States Political Adviser for Japan, writes to the Secretary of State regarding secret airmail instruction No. 200 transmitting a Swedish Foreign Office request for interrogatories to be put to General Makoto Onodera. Atcheson explains that Onodera had already been exhaustively interrogated by intelligence officers, culminating in a Top Secret SSU/CIG report dated July 20, 1946. GHQ CINCAFPAC intelligence officers advised that it was inadvisable to interrogate Onodera further and confirmed that the Swedish inquiries could be fully resolved from the existing interrogation report.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 705 from George Atcheson, Jr., on Request for Interrogation of General Onodera

subfiles.about: Cover memorandum transmitting three Central Intelligence Group intelligence reports based on the interrogation of General Makoto Onodera to the Department of State.
subfiles.from: Chief, Dissemination Branch, Central Intelligence Group (Colford)
subfiles.summary: The Chief of the Dissemination Branch of the Central Intelligence Group forwards three intelligence reports (DB-1244, DB-1245, and DB-1247) obtained from a reliable source to Jack Neal in the Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State. The memorandum notes that the material is forwarded in the belief that it will be of interest. It instructs that any replies or couriers concerning the dissemination be referred directly to I. C. Houck.
subfiles.title: CIG Memorandum Transmitting Interrogation Reports DB-1244, DB-1245, and DB-1247
subfiles.to: Jack Neal (Division of Foreign Activity Correlation, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Intelligence report contrasting General Onodera's account of May–July 1945 Swedish peace mediation feelers with the version recorded by Allied operative Eric Erickson.
subfiles.summary: This Central Intelligence Group report details Major General Makoto Onodera's statements during his interrogation at Sugamo Prison regarding Swedish attempts to initiate peace negotiations between Japan and the Western Allies in May and July 1945. Onodera claimed that Swedish businessman Eric Erickson approached him proposing that Prince Carl of the Swedish Red Cross mediate peace discussions, but Onodera declined to initiate them without official instructions from Tokyo. When the Swedish Foreign Office subsequently approached Japanese Minister Suemasa Okamoto in July, Tokyo rejected the initiative, leading to conflict between Okamoto and Onodera. An appended intelligence note contrasts this with Erickson's contemporaneous report as an Allied agent, which indicated that Onodera actively sought Prince Carl's intervention to avoid national destruction, while claiming exclusive authority to negotiate.
subfiles.title: CIG Report DB-1244: Onodera's Version of Swedish Offers to Initiate Peace Negotiations
subfiles.to: G-2, CINCAFPAC; ID-WDGS; ONI; Department of State

subfiles.about: Intelligence report detailing the organizational structure, authority lines, intelligence targets, and special sabotage missions of Japanese military attachés in Europe.
subfiles.summary: Based on General Onodera's interrogation at Sugamo Prison, this report provides a comprehensive breakdown of Japanese wartime military missions in Europe representing the Army General Staff, Arms Administration Directorate, Air Force, and War Ministry Political Bureau. It describes the chains of command and intelligence reporting directed by Department II of the General Staff, as well as the geographical distribution of intelligence targets focusing initially on the USSR and later shifting to the Western Allies. The report also reveals three secret directives issued to the Berlin attaché, including joint Japanese-Abwehr subversive and sabotage operations against the Soviet Ukraine and Caucasus involving exile figure Bamat and Abwehr Amt II.
subfiles.title: CIG Report DB-1245: Japanese Wartime Military Missions in Europe
subfiles.to: G-2, CINCAFPAC; ID-WDGS; ONI; Department of State

subfiles.about: Intelligence report documenting the clandestine background, intelligence ties, and European activities of Japanese journalist Momotaro Enomoto.
subfiles.summary: This report compiles General Onodera's debriefing statements concerning Mainichi/Nichi-Nichi correspondent Momotaro Enomoto, who arrived in Stockholm in early 1945 after operating in Turkey and Hungary. Enomoto claimed allegiance to right-wing nationalist political fixer Han Wakabayashi and sought Onodera's assistance to set up radio communications for an Abwehr network under Richard Kauder (Klatt) intending to infiltrate the United States. Onodera suspected Enomoto and Klatt were using intelligence operations as cover for black-market activities and postwar safehaven preparations, but acknowledged that Enomoto possessed extraordinary linguistic and espionage abilities, having successfully penetrated German Abwehr and Hungarian intelligence circles.
subfiles.title: CIG Report DB-1247: Momotaro Enomoto
subfiles.to: G-2, CINCAFPAC; ID-WDGS; ONI; Department of State
